title: Find an escalation loop
description:
Each support agent escalates tickets to exactly one other person, or to nobody. A misconfiguration can create a loop where a ticket bounces around forever.

You are given `escalates_to`, a dictionary from each person to the person they escalate to (or `None`), and a `start` person. Write `has_loop(escalates_to, start)` that returns `True` if following escalations from `start` ever revisits someone.

Everyone who appears as a value is also a key.

**Example**

```
has_loop({"ana": "ben", "ben": "cy", "cy": "ana"}, "ana")    # True
has_loop({"ana": "ben", "ben": None}, "ana")                 # False
```
hints: Follow the pointers one step at a time and remember everyone you have visited.
If you reach `None`, there is no loop. If you reach someone already visited, there is.
Stretch: do it with no extra memory using two walkers, one moving one step at a time and one moving two. If there is a loop, the fast one catches the slow one.
